title: Human Origins, Language & Religion
subtitle: Deep Dive Audio Series • Origins of Speech, Proto-Writing, Big Gods & Human Civilization

sections.heading: Origins of Speech, Paleopathology of Care, Body Lexicons & Cuneiform Mind

episodes.label: The Enzyme That Changed the Fatty Acid Map — FADS1/FADS2 Haplotypes, Delta-5/Delta-6 Desaturase Cytochrome b5 Electron Transfer, [U-13C]ALA Conversion & Greenlandic Selection
episodes.notes: From European lipidomic GWAS of phosphatidylcholine PC 36:4 across FADS1/FADS2 haplotypes A and D (Ameur et al. 2012) to front-end delta-6/delta-5 desaturase HPGG cytochrome b5 architecture, Gillingham et al. [U-13C]ALA tracer recovery in plasma [13C]EPA (3.77% vs. 0.89% at 48h), and Greenlandic Inuit vs. ancient European selection scans (Fumagalli 2015; Mathieson 2018, 2020).

episodes.label: The Shell With a Second Life — Marine Shell Personal Ornaments, Use-Wear Microscopy, Ochre Residue & Middle Stone Age Symbolic Exchange
episodes.notes: Taphonomic and microscopic reconstruction of Paleolithic perforated shell ornaments: distinguishing natural marine predation and wave abrasion from human suspension wear, stringing facets, ochre residue, and long-distance inland transport.

episodes.label: The Scroll That Stayed Rolled — Virtual Unwrapping from En-Gedi's Metal-Bearing Ink (Seales 2016) to Herculaneum Carbon Ink (Parker 2019) & Complete Surface Reading of PHerc. 1667 & Philodemus's On Gods Book 8
episodes.notes: X-ray micro-CT virtual unwrapping and machine-learned carbon-ink detection in carbonized ancient scrolls: Seales et al.'s (2016) reading of Leviticus inside the charred En-Gedi scroll, Parker et al.'s (2019) 3D voxel ink classification on Herculaneum fragment PHerc. Paris 2 Fr. 96, and Angelotti et al.'s (2026 preprint) end-to-end surface reconstruction of PHerc. 1667 and title identification of Philodemus's On Gods Book 8 in PHerc. 139.

episodes.label: The Paint Beneath the Stone — Uranium-Thorium Calcite Dating, Sulawesi & Iberian Cave Art Stratigraphy & Pleistocene Pigment Chemistry
episodes.notes: Archaeometric dating and chemical characterization of Pleistocene cave art beneath carbonate speleothem crusts: laser-ablation U-Th minimum age constraints in Sulawesi and Iberia, ochre/manganese pigment recipes, and stratigraphic cross-sections.

episodes.label: Nine Thousand Years at Oakhurst — Holocene Southern African Ancient Genomes, Deep Genetic Continuity & Later Stone Age Shifts
episodes.notes: Ancient DNA time-transect from the Oakhurst rock shelter in southern Africa (Gretzinger et al. 2024; Jakobsson et al. 2026): 10,000 years of Holocene San-related genetic continuity followed by late-Holocene pastoralist and Iron Age gene flow.

episodes.label: When Maize Moved — Ancient Teosinte Introgression, Highland Adaptation & the Archaeological Dispersal of Corn
episodes.notes: Archaeobotanical, paleogenomic, and isotopic reconstruction of maize domestication: Balsas teosinte divergence, Mexicana highland introgression, microbotanical phytolith/starch clocks, and dietary transitions across the Americas.

episodes.label: A Jaw From the Missing Chapter — Paleoproteomics, Mandibular Morphology & Middle Pleistocene Hominin Lineages
episodes.notes: Paleoanthropological and paleoproteomic investigation of a fossil hominin mandible where ancient DNA failed: enamel/dentine collagen peptide mass fingerprinting, morphometric geometry, and what a single bone can and cannot resolve.

episodes.label: The Islands Kept Their Words — Teouma Lapita Ancient Genomes in Vanuatu, Near-Complete Papuan Ancestry Turnover & Why Austronesian Oceanic Languages Persisted
episodes.notes: Reconciling ancient genomics, Lapita dentate-stamped pottery, and historical linguistics in Remote Oceania: why 3,000-year-old Teouma individuals carried minimal Papuan ancestry, how subsequent migration transformed Vanuatu's gene pool without replacing its Austronesian Oceanic languages, and why pots, genes, and words move along distinct historical channels.

episodes.label: The Dogs Before the Map — Lawyer's Cave Coastal Alaska Femur, Koster & Stilwell II Intentional Dog Burials (~10,000 BP), Swan Point & Beringian Canids & Pre-Contact Indigenous American Dog Genomes
episodes.notes: Zooarchaeology, radiocarbon reservoir effects, and paleogenomics of early dogs in the Americas: da Silva Coelho et al. (2021) Lawyer's Cave southeast Alaska femur fragment and marine dietary offset, Perri et al.'s directly dated Koster and Stilwell II Illinois dog burials (~10,190-9,630 cal BP), Lanoë et al. (2024) Swan Point subarctic salmon-fed canids, Graf et al. (2026) Beringian base camp, and Ní Leathlobhair et al. (2018) pre-contact American dog clade.

episodes.label: The Cargo That Had Many Homes — The 14th-Century BCE Uluburun Shipwreck, Cypriot Oxhide Copper Ingots, Central Asian Mushiston vs. Anatolian Tin Isotopes & Egyptian Cobalt-Blue Glass Cakes
episodes.notes: Provenance chemistry of the Late Bronze Age Uluburun shipwreck (~1320 BCE): Cypriot lead-isotope signatures in 354 oxhide copper ingots, Egyptian trace-element fingerprints in 175 raw glass ingots, and the geochemical debate (Powell et al. 2022 vs. Berger et al. 2023) over Central Asian Mushiston vs. Anatolian tin isotopes and anthropogenic lead contamination.

episodes.label: The Canoes Under the Lake — Neolithic La Marmotta Submerged Dugouts, Transverse Hull Ribs, Mysterious T-Shaped Rigging Toggles & Prehistoric Mediterranean Crossings
episodes.notes: Archaeological and nautical analysis of the five Early Neolithic dugout canoes submerged in Lake Bracciano at La Marmotta (Gibaja et al. 2024): deliberate multi-species wood selection (oak, alder, poplar, beech), integral transverse hull ribs, enigmatic T-shaped mortised wooden objects along the gunwale, radiocarbon wiggle-matching, and experimental open-water Mediterranean voyages.

episodes.label: The Cacao in the Clay — 5,300-Year-Old Upper Amazon Cacao Starch, Theobromine & Ancient DNA at Santa Ana–La Florida (Zarrillo 2018), Honduran Beverage Vessels (Henderson 2007) & Pre-Columbian Dispersal Genomics
episodes.notes: Archaeobotany, chemical residue analysis, and archaeogenomics of early Theobroma cacao: Zarrillo et al.'s (2018) triple-line identification of starch grains, theobromine, and ancient DNA in ~5,300-year-old Mayo-Chinchipe ceramic vessels at Santa Ana–La Florida (Ecuador), Henderson et al.'s (2007) Puerto Escondido Honduran spouted vessels before 1000 BCE, Cornejo et al.'s (2018) Criollo domestication genomics, and Lanaud et al.'s (2024) pre-Columbian Ceramic residue dispersal survey.

episodes.label: The Family Beneath the Long Barrow — Early Neolithic Chambered Tomb Pedigrees, Five-Generation Kinship & Ancient DNA at Hazleton North
episodes.notes: High-resolution ancient DNA kinship reconstruction of 35 individuals from the 5,700-year-old Hazleton North long barrow (Fowler et al. 2021): a five-generation extended family pedigree, patrilineal continuity, four reproductive women with shared male partners, and spatial mapping across north and south L-shaped chambers.

episodes.label: When Polynesia Met South America — Pre-Columbian Sweet Potato Genetics, Rapa Nui Voyaging & Trans-Pacific Contact
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (When Polynesia Met South America): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

episodes.label: Animal Signals, Orality & Silicon Minds — Evolutionary Syntax Boundaries, Pre-Literate Memory & Large Language Models
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (How AI and Neural Implants Rewrite Language): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

episodes.label: First Cities & the Fertile Crescent — Urban Epistemology, Polycentric Domestication & Ancient Philology
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (From Neanderthals to the First Alphabet): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

episodes.label: Proto-Writing, Tokens & True Script — Jiahu Symbols, Danube Notation, Near Eastern Calculi & Sumerian Cuneiform
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (How Ancient Accountants Invented Writing): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

episodes.label: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
episodes.notes: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

episodes.label: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency
episodes.notes: Perceptual narrowing in infant speech acquisition: Werker & Tees (1984) preservation of English contrasts alongside loss of non-native Hindi/Salish discrimination by 10–12 months, Maye, Werker & Gerken (2002) statistical bimodal vs. unimodal distribution reshaping, Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003) live vs. televised Mandarin tutors, and Lytle, Garcia-Sierra & Kuhl (2018) peer-paired contingent video.

episodes.label: The Floor That Kept the Dead — Neolithic Çatalhöyük Subfloor Burials (Haddow 2025), Shifting Intra-Building Genetic Kinship Across 1,000 Years (63% to 22%, Yaka 2021 & Yüncü 2025) & Maternal Lineage Ties
episodes.notes: Stratigraphic bioarchaeology and ancient DNA of subfloor house burials across Neolithic Anatolia: Haddow et al.'s (2025) house-life-cycle burial patterns at Çatalhöyük (including Building 42's foundation burial), Yaka et al.'s (2021) transition from biological kin burials at Aşıklı Höyük/Boncuklu to co-burial of unrelated individuals, and Yüncü et al.'s (2025) 131-genome time series revealing declining intra-building genetic kinship (63% -> 30% -> 22%), maternal house linkages, and female subadult grave goods.

episodes.label: The Opening That Stayed Open — Copper Age Pontecagnano Cranial Trepanation, Beveled Scraping Remodeling, Femoral Osteomyelitis & Modern CT Margins of Healed Skull Defects
episodes.notes: Osteological and radiological investigation of the 5,000-year-old Copper Age trepanned skull from Pontecagnano, southern Italy (Petrone et al.): broad watch-face outer scraping tapering to a lentil-sized inner aperture, obliterated diploic pores and smooth remodeled margins proving extended survival, severe femoral osteomyelitis in the same individual, and modern surgical CT correlates.

episodes.label: The Medicine We Cannot See — El Sidrón Neanderthal Dental Calculus Pyrolysis-GC/MS & aDNA, Chamomile/Yarrow/Poplar/Penicillium vs. Dental Abscess & Experimental Calculus Entrapment
episodes.notes: Bioarchaeological and experimental critique of prehistoric non-nutritive plant ingestion: El Sidrón Neanderthal dental calculus pyrolysis-GC/MS and shotgun metagenomics alongside a mandibular dental abscess and Enterocytozoon bieneusi infection (Hardy et al. 2012; Weyrich et al. 2017), experimental herbal mouth-rinse calculus entrapment models, and the evidentiary boundary between dietary/craft/environmental exposure and intentional self-medication.

episodes.label: When Stroke Steals Words vs. Meaning — Broca's 'Tan,' Sign-Language Aphasia & Inner Silence
episodes.notes: Traces Broca's 1861 autopsy of Leborgne (and 2007 3T MRI re-scanning), Salk Institute ASL stroke dissociations, corollary discharge, and anendophasia.

sections.heading: Big Gods, Sacred Violence, Rituals & Evolution of Civilization

episodes.label: Which God Do You Turn To When Food Might Run Short? — Cross-Cultural Food-Worry Horizons, Moralistic vs. Local Deities & Christchurch Earthquake Panels
episodes.notes: Statistical and anthropological evaluation of material insecurity and religious commitment (Baimel et al. 2022 across 14 populations; Purzycki et al. 2018; Sibley & Bulbulia 2012 Canterbury earthquake longitudinal panel).

episodes.label: Can a God Be Fooled? — Developmental False-Belief Tasks, Barrett's Cracker Box, Yukatek Maya Interviews & Omniscience vs. Moral Policing
episodes.notes: Developmental cognitive science of supernatural minds: unexpected-contents false-belief tasks (Barrett et al. 2001; Knight et al. Yukatek Maya; Lane et al. preparedness vs. anthropomorphism) and separating epistemic omniscience from moral policing across development.

episodes.label: The Seal and the Crack — Mohenjo-daro Seal DK5175/143, Shang Oracle Bone Ping 0368 & What Ritual Surfaces Preserve
episodes.notes: Comparative material epistemology of ancient religion: what an undeciphered Mohenjo-daro steatite stamp seal (DK5175/143) vs. a dated Late Shang pyro-osteomantic turtle plastron inscription (Ping 0368) can and cannot prove about supernatural agency and ritual rules.

episodes.label: When the Metronome Stops — Behavioral Synchrony vs. Shared Intentionality, Fire-Walking Heart-Rate Coupling & Public-Goods Triads
episodes.notes: Experimental dissection of collective ritual mechanics: Reddish, Fischer & Bulbulia's (2013) n = 82 triad foot-pedal experiments separating passive metronome synchrony from mutually adjusted shared intentionality, alongside Konvalinka et al.'s fire-walking heart-rate recurrence plots.

episodes.label: The Water Temple's Calendar — Balinese Subak Irrigation Networks, Lansing & Kremer's Pest-vs.-Water Tradeoff Models & Green Revolution Disruption
episodes.notes: Systems ecology and historical ethnography of Balinese water temples (Lansing 1987, Lansing & Kremer 1993): how ritual cropping calendars balance upstream water scarcity against synchronized fallow pest control, what the 1970s Green Revolution natural experiment revealed, and critiques from historical archival records.

episodes.label: The Stranger in the Sharing Game — Cross-Cultural Random Allocation Games, Moralizing Gods & Impartial Rule Following
episodes.notes: Methodological and statistical audit of cross-cultural Random Allocation Games (Purzycki et al.): how die-roll coin allocations measure impartial rule-following toward distant co-religionists and what the binomial model can and cannot prove.

episodes.label: What the Ritual Cost — Extreme Rituals, Pain, Heart-Rate Synchrony & Prosocial Donation Experiments
episodes.notes: Field experiments on high-ordeal vs. low-ordeal religious rituals (Xygalatas et al.; Konvalinka et al.): physiological arousal, pain ratings, spectator-performer heart-rate coupling, and anonymous charitable donations.

episodes.label: What the Neighbors Could See — Credibility Enhancing Displays (CREDs), Public Ritual Observability & Cooperative Trust
episodes.notes: Empirical and evolutionary analysis of observable religious behavior: how public ritual attendance, visible taboos, and Credibility Enhancing Displays (CREDs) solve the cultural transmission problem and shape inter-personal trust among neighbors.

episodes.label: The Feast in the Ground — Durrington Walls Near Stonehenge (~2500 BCE), Roasted Pig Bones vs. Dairy/Beef Grooved-Ware Lipids, Multi-Isotope Livestock Mobility & Coprolite Parasites
episodes.notes: Multi-proxy archaeological forensics at Durrington Walls (~2500 BCE): resolving the pig-bone vs. cattle/dairy potsherd lipid paradox through culinary segregation (Craig et al. 2015), five-isotope British livestock provenance (Madgwick et al. 2019), and Mitchell's coprolite paleoparasitology showing poorly cooked bovine/canid-shared tapeworm and capillariid infections.

episodes.label: The Eyes on the Wall — Bateson's Honesty-Box Coffee Experiment, Watching-Eyes Meta-Analyses & Replication Boundaries
episodes.notes: Critical audit of the watching-eyes literature from Bateson et al. (2006) breakroom coffee honesty-box study to large-sample preregistered replications and meta-analyses.

episodes.label: The Commune That Outlasted Its Neighbors — 19th-Century Religious vs. Secular Communes, Costly Requirements & Survival Hazard Models
episodes.notes: Quantitative survival analysis of 200 nineteenth-century U.S. communes (Sosis & Bressler 2003): how costly taboos and behavioral restrictions correlate with commune longevity differently in religious versus secular communities.

episodes.label: Who Knew What Was in the Box — Epistemic Access, Secret Ritual Objects, Theory-of-Mind Asymmetries & Religious Authority
episodes.notes: Cognitive and anthropological analysis of hidden ritual contents, asymmetrical epistemic access, and how experiments separate ordinary human false-belief reasoning from attributions of supernatural omniscience.

episodes.label: The Blank Cell in the Big Gods Debate — Seshat Missing-Data Coding, Chronological Priors & Retraction Reanalysis
episodes.notes: Epistemological and statistical dissection of the Seshat Big Gods controversy: how coding unknown historical cells as zeros shifted the inferred appearance of moralizing gods relative to social complexity, and why absence of evidence, documented absence, and first attestation are distinct.
